messages.author: 5c009c55dafaeed0
messages.subject: predict in pcountOpen
parts:
Hi All,

I'm running some models using pcountOpen, and would like to predict abundance per pixel in my study area.  I think it might be faster to use the raster calculator in ArcGIS to do this, and so am trying to figure out what equation to enter that would match what the predict function is doing in R.  I tried the predict function using a data frame containing only a single line of data, and got a predicted abundance of 5.7.  Then I extracted the coefficients from the model, and tried to predict abundance using the same covariate values, but this time I got an abundance of 8.9.  Can anyone tell me what, exactly, the predict function is doing? And is it possible to replicate this without using the predict function? My model and the code I tried is below.

Thanks!

Lucretia 

#model 
jr5 <- pcountOpen(~ h_shrub1k + d2srl, ~1, ~1, ~ewind+etemp+time, data=jr.umf, mixture="ZIP", K=30, se=T)

#results from using predict
> newdata <- data.frame(h_shrub1k=18.660,d2srl=factor("201",levels=c("0","31","33","37","38","46","77","201")))
> predict(jr5, newdata=newdata, type="lambda")
  Predicted SE lower upper
1  5.712804 NA    NA    NA

#results from extracting coefficients and multiplying by covariates
> jrcoef <- coef(jr5)
> jrcoef 
      lam(Int) lam(h_shrub1k)   lam(d2srl31)   lam(d2srl33)   lam(d2srl37)   lam(d2srl38)   lam(d2srl46) 
    3.67315759    -0.06703627   -12.81893066    -3.10963438    -1.18704957   -14.45589704    -9.37114394 
  lam(d2srl77)  lam(d2srl201)  gamConst(Int)     omega(Int)         p(Int)       p(ewind)       p(etemp) 
   -0.30894673    -0.23041692    -0.04167141    12.07326965    -2.58426177    -0.02684577     0.01755272 
       p(time)       psi(psi) 
   -8.67658032    -0.56747637 
> jrcoef <- jrcoef[c("lam(Int)","lam(h_shrub1k)","lam(d2srl201)")]
> jrcoef 
      lam(Int) lam(h_shrub1k)  lam(d2srl201) 
    3.67315759    -0.06703627    -0.23041692 
> nd2 <- cbind(1,18.660, 1)
> test <- nd2%*%(jrcoef)
> exp(test)
         [,1]
[1,] 8.951704

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] predict in pcountOpen
parts:
Hi Lucretia,

For the ZIP model, predict(..., type="lambda") is returning the
expected value of N[i,1], which is lambda[i]*(1-psi):

> 8.951704*(1-plogis(-0.567))
[1] 5.71182

I can see how this might be confusing.

Richard
